$comment: The one home for every number and enum a Refract rule enforces. Rules cite the id (THR-…) instead of restating the value; scripts/lint-rule-literals.sh fails a NEW numeric literal in a MUST rule that does not cite one (ratchet). JSON, not YAML: the consumers are python3 standard-library scripts (gate-check.py, standards-check.py, the lints) and the model; nothing in a user's repo parses YAML, and a hand-rolled YAML subset fails silently — the same reason .claude/gates.json is JSON. A project overrides a value in .claude/thresholds.local.json with the same id; an override may TIGHTEN a floor ("floor": true) and never loosen it (templates/governance/precedence.md § 2). Each entry: value (number, string or object), unit, floor (true = a project may only tighten), owner (the catalog row or rule that applies it), why.

THR-RES-TIMEOUT.why: an external call with no timeout cascades; 2 s is a default for in-region calls, never a ceiling the caller's own budget cannot fit

never_on: a non-idempotent write without an idempotency key

THR-RES-RETRY.why: 429 is a back-off signal, not a terminal 4xx: retry it no sooner than Retry-After (precedence A7); unbounded attempts turn a provider storm into a bill or a ban

value.floor: exact decimal DECIMAL(p,s) or integer minor units, always with a currency; never float

THR-MONEY.why: DATA-9 is the floor; inside the payment and ledger domains integer minor units win (precedence A14)

THR-ERR-ENVELOPE.why: one envelope mapped in one place; public APIs document it as their contract

THR-PAGINATION.why: every list has a default and a hard maximum; offset past ~1000 rescans rows on most engines

THR-PASSWORD-HASH.why: the algorithm name is not the control, the parameters are (OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet minimums)

THR-TOKEN-TTL.why: short-lived credentials bound the blast radius of a leak

THR-CACHE-TTL.why: an explicit TTL with jitter avoids a synchronized expiry stampede

THR-PERF-REGRESSION.why: a delta inside the noise band is NO-CHANGE; a measured regression past the threshold is a FAIL unless waived

value.changed_lines: ratchet — never below the project's declared floor

THR-COVERAGE.why: a ratchet, not a magic number: the project declares the floor

THR-MUTATION.why: diff-scoped mutation proves the tests would notice the change being wrong

THR-NIT-CAP.why: more nits bury the Important findings; after round 1 only Important findings post

THR-LOOP.why: a third non-converging pass is an upstream problem; escalate to a human with the ledger

THR-WAIVER.why: an expired waiver is a FAIL

THR-FN-LEN.owner: the project's linter config (max-lines-per-function / funlen / PLR0915 / …)
THR-FN-LEN.why: there is no portable function-length number; the project's configured linter value is the rule (precedence A5). With no linter configured the length rule is advisory, never a hard FAIL

THR-COMPLEXITY.why: same as THR-FN-LEN: read the configured value; a change may not raise it beyond the touched file's baseline

THR-DRY.why: a second copy of something that already exists reuses it; a NEW shared abstraction waits for the third occurrence (precedence A28)

THR-TODO.why: an owner and a date make a TODO expire; a ticket alone does not (precedence A2)

THR-LOG-LEVEL.why: a recovered catch logs at warn so the recovery is visible in production (precedence A9)

THR-CLAUDE-MD-LINES.why: code.claude.com memory docs: target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md; longer files cost context and reduce adherence

THR-ALWAYS-ON-TOKENS.why: always-on rules and CLAUDE.md are paid on every turn before the user types

THR-DESC-BUDGET.why: descriptions are routing text paid before anyone asks; over the platform budget descriptions are truncated to names
